title: Latency-weighted Ticket Rebalancer for Continuous Batcher
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Improves continuous batcher fairness under mixed KV-heavy and latency-sensitive workloads by introducing a latency-weighted ticket rebalancer. Backward compatible and feature-gated; rollout via canary.
description:
Context and motivation:
Mixed workloads exposed a recurrent starvation mode where long-running KV-heavy requests accumulated ticket reservations and prevented latency-sensitive short requests from accessing low-latency slots. Existing ticketing logic prioritizes SLA bands but lacks an explicit mechanism to rebalance tickets when wait-time contributes more to customer impact than nominal priority.

What this PR does (single-string description):
- Adds a latency-weighted ticket rebalancer in the continuous batcher scheduler that periodically scans the ticket pools and moves a bounded number of tickets from low-urgency queues to higher-urgency lanes when historical wait-time indicates impending starvation. The rebalancer computes a moving expected-wait impact score per ticket using recent per-route token latency histograms and a decay factor to avoid oscillation.
- Integrates KV-cache hint signals so tickets currently holding KV pins are deprioritized for rebalance unless they have exceeded a configurable hold TTL. This prevents breaking KV-prefetch semantics while still allowing long-stalled pins to be re-evaluated.
- Adds a soft cooldown and jitter to rebalance actions to prevent thundering reassignments across hosts.
- Exposes new metrics: continuous_batcher.rebalance_actions, continuous_batcher.rebalance_skipped_due_to_kv_pin, continuous_batcher.rebalance_latency_score_percentiles.
- Adds a new feature flag and runtime config: rebalance.enabled (default: false), rebalance.scan_interval_ms, rebalance.max_moves_per_scan, rebalance.decay_half_life_ms, rebalance.kv_pin_ttl_ms, rebalance.cooldown_jitter_ms.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Approach favors empirical latency impact over static priority escalation to avoid amplifying noisy priorities in mixed QPS environments.
- Decay term reduces oscillation vs strict aging strategies (we avoid moving tickets back-and-forth inside a single host).
- We do not alter core ticket reservation model; rebalance is a best-effort transfer of ticket ownership within a host. Cross-host ticket migration is intentionally out-of-scope for this change.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for rebalancer scoring, cooldown logic, and KV-pin interaction added in scheduler/rebalancer_test.go.
- Microbench harness: bench/rebalancer_mixed_workload.go reproduces a 70/30 KV:latency-sensitive mix and shows 40-60% reduction in starvation counts in canary sims.
- Canary plan: enable rebalance.enabled=true on 5% of single-tenant Dedicated pools for 48 hours and monitor continuous_batcher.rebalance_actions and p95_token_latency. Rollback if p95 increases more than 5% or error rate increases.

- [x] Canary rollout plan documented

conversation: Arjun Patel (reviewer): Can we get a short justification for the decay half-life chosen? Do you have sensitivity runs?

Maya Chen (author): Added a note in the design doc and included sensitivity graphs in bench output. Default half-life (30s) came from sims where shorter half-lives caused oscillation under bursty traffic.
Leila Gomez (reviewer): Race condition concern when moving tickets while the ticket owner is about to start the kernel. Suggest checking reservation state atomically and using a short grace window.
Maya Chen: Implemented an atomic reservation check and a 50ms grace window. Added tests that assert no double-assignment during concurrent start().
Tomás Rivera (approver): Verified local perf runs; metrics look good and no regressions on p50/p95. Approving for merge after CI green.
